fact: ELECAM says it is deduplicating the biometric voter registry, which holds around 8.2 million registered voters, and has issued biometric voter cards (Biometric Update).
ELECAM announced in May 2025 that it took delivery of new biometric gear to support voter registration for the presidential election (Biometric Update).
ELECAM presented 1,000 new third-generation biometric enrolment kits on 7 May 2025, with trainer training held 7 to 11 May before deployment to communal branches (Le Jour).

Le Jour reports that after the 2024 registration campaign ELECAM decided to integrate thousands of citizens, previously not recorded because of a fingerprint problem, into the national electoral file.

Opposition politician Maurice Kamto said thousands of names were expunged from Cameroon's national voter register in a December 2024 database clean-up over rejected fingerprints, about 12,000 voters according to the article, and ELECAM launched its 2025 annual biometric voter registration cycle on 6 January aiming for at least eight million names.
